Credits and usage

Read your balance, your spending limits and the usage behind a bill.

Money is held in wallets and counted in mu, the unit of account. Today the balance and the spending page are session doors of the console, not relay-key doors:

GET /api/me/wallets

Who may call: signed-in session; roles: admin, cfo_viewer, fde, hr_ops, manager, member, operator.

Response schema

{
  "description": "Hand-written, read against me_wallets in crates/mr-server/src/routes.rs and WalletRow in crates/mr-kernel/src/wallets.rs. A session credential. A person with no personal workspace yet gets an empty list, not an error. Amounts are in mu (the unit of account).",

A wallet has a balance and an amount held; a spending cap has a period, a limit and what is spent so far, and a forecast of the day it runs out. A person can pause spending, and the page lists the runs a pause skipped.

Budgets degrade before they block

When a budget runs out the router first lowers autonomy or files a request for help; a hard stop comes after. When a request does stop for money it answers 402; see Errors.

For a key holder: four doors under /v1

These doors take the relay key itself as the bearer, exactly as the completion doors do, and only read. A revoked, expired or unknown key is refused with the same 401 as everywhere else. They read the key's own ledgers: a decision of another key or another workspace is a 404, never a 403. Each costs one request against the key's rate limit.

curl https://relay.massrelay.ai/v1/key -H "Authorization: Bearer mrk_<prefix>_<secret>"

Response schema

    "prefix",

GET /v1/usage

Who may call: relay key (bearer).

Response schema

{
  "description": "Read against crates/mr-gateway/src/key_doors.rs `usage_body`. Query: from, to (ISO date or datetime, default the UTC calendar month), end_user (one tag), group_by=end_user (one row per tag).",
  "type": "object",
  "required": [
    "object",
    "unit",
    "period",
    "requests",
    "inputTokens",
    "outputTokens",
    "costMu"
  ],
  "properties": {
    "object": {
      "const": "usage"
    },
    "unit": {
      "const": "mu"
    },
    "period": {
      "type": "object",
      "required": [
        "from",
        "to"
      ],
      "properties": {
        "from": {
          "type": "string"
        },
        "to": {
          "type": "string"
        }
      }
    },
    "endUser": {
      "type": "string"
    },
    "requests": {
      "type": "integer"
    },
    "inputTokens": {
      "type": "integer"
    },
    "outputTokens": {
      "type": "integer"
    },
    "costMu": {
      "type": "integer",
      "description": "micro-dollars, the unit of account"
    },
    "byEndUser": {
      "type": "array",
      "items": {
        "type": "object",
        "required": [
          "endUser",
          "requests",
          "inputTokens",
          "outputTokens",
          "costMu"
        ],
        "properties": {
          "endUser": {
            "type": "string"
          },
          "requests": {
            "type": "integer"
          },
          "inputTokens": {
            "type": "integer"
          },
          "outputTokens": {
            "type": "integer"
          },
          "costMu": {
            "type": "integer",
            "description": "micro-dollars, the unit of account"
          }
        }
      }
    }
  }
}

The rollup of the key's ledger rows for a period: requests, tokens and cost. from and to take an ISO date or datetime (default: this UTC calendar month); end_user narrows to one end-user tag; group_by=end_user returns one row per tag.

curl "https://relay.massrelay.ai/v1/usage?group_by=end_user" -H "Authorization: Bearer mrk_<prefix>_<secret>"

Rate-limit headers

Every /v1 answer whose request reached the rate limiter carries the state of the limit that binds that key, read from the same evaluation that admitted the request (a header never costs a second slot).

| header | meaning | |---|---| | X-RateLimit-Limit | requests per minute of the binding limit (the key's, or its workspace's if that is tighter) | | X-RateLimit-Remaining | whole requests still admitted right now without being queued | | X-RateLimit-Reset | seconds, rounded up, until one more request would be admitted without queueing (0 while some remain) | | Retry-After | on a 429 only: seconds to wait, rounded up |

When no limit is configured for the key or its workspace, the three X-RateLimit-* headers are not sent. The same headers ride on streamed answers and on the 429.
